newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey has 655,000 T grain in government stocks.
newsitem.headline: Turkey has 655,000 T grain in government stocks.

text.p: Turkey's state grain board (TMO) has 655,000 tonnes of grain, mostly wheat, in its stocks, which include emergency stocks for the army, TMO General Manager Ismet Agan said on Thursday.
He told a parliamentary commission the TMO's total stocks as of June 1 included 466,000 tonnes of wheat, 126,000 tonnes of barley, 25,000 tonnes of corn and 22,000 tonnes of paddy.
"Of the total wheat stocks, 178,000 tonnes are reserved for the Turkish Armed Forces," he told the commission.

He said the TMO, the government's grain purchasing agent, planned to buy a total of 3.775 million tonnes of grain in 1997/98, which includes 2.2 million tonnes of wheat, one million tonnes barley, 400,000 tonnes corn, 100,000 tonnes rye, 40,000 tonnes paddy and 20,000 tonnes of oats.
It bought a total of nearly 1.6 million tonnes of grain in the previous year.
"The TMO needs 130 trillion lira ($912.3 million) for its planned purchases and all preparations were made to meet the financing," he said, without giving details.

Treasury officials said they would seek a $250 million syndicated loan, probably this month or in July, to meet part of the money. Officials have said the TMO will use domestic sources for the rest of the required funds.
Agan said the TMO was considering selling 2.087 million tonnes of grain domestically to "regulate the market", but he did not break down the figure. --Ercan Ersoy, Ankara newsroom, 90-312-4462940
